title: Nottingham Forest freeze season ticket prices for 2026-27
content:
Nottingham Forest have frozen season ticket prices for the 2026-2027 campaign.

Vitor Pereira’s side have nine games left to preserve their Premier League status, ahead of Sunday’s home game against Fulham.

Forest, who are level on points with 18th-placed West Ham United, will desperately hope to remain in the top flight but, regardless of whether they do return to the second tier for the first time since 2022, there will be no increase in prices.

The club have also listened to concerns expressed by fans about the next generation of supporters being frozen out, by reintroducing the ‘young adult’ category of season ticket for those aged 18-21. More than 1,000 supporters could save £300 a year through this initiative.

“We have listened carefully, and we have acted in a way that we hope will reaffirm the bond between the club and its fans,” Forest chairman Nicholas Randall said in a release. “That sense of togetherness — the feeling that we are all pulling in the same direction — has always been at the heart of what makes Forest unique, and we are committed to strengthening that as we look ahead with ambition and belief.”

Forest will surely have been aware of the value of some positive PR in a season when there has been plenty to be critical of.

Make no mistake, freezing season ticket prices is a positive step from a club that has not historically shied away from raising them. But following a campaign that has seen Vitor Pereira become the fourth permanent manager since September, the fans deserve some reward for their patience amid the chaos. It feels like a wise decision from the Forest hierarchy.

In April 2024, Forest increased season ticket prices by an average of 24 per cent. Many viewed it as being a misstep, as a move that would heavily impact fans, without significantly affecting the club’s bank balance at the same time.

It was a decision that would have generated roughly £2.5million ($3.35m) of additional income over the course of the 2024-2025 season. Forest’s revenue during the previous 2023-2024 campaign had been £154.8m.

This time last year, there was a round of more modest increases, with the most expensive season ticket going from £850 to £915 and the cheapest rising from £550 to £575. Again, there was criticism, although it was largely lessened by the fact that Nuno Espirito Santo’s side were, at that stage of the campaign, fighting for Champions League qualification.

As fans debate whether to renew now, there is again a question mark hanging over the club, as Pereira battles to lead Forest clear of the threat of relegation. But while they sweat over the prospect of a return to the Championship, they simultaneously have an outside chance of securing Champions League football, if they can follow in​​ Tottenham Hotspur’s footsteps by combining a Premier League struggle with lifting the Europa League trophy in May.

This season was meant to be an adventure, as Forest returned to European football for the first time in three decades. It still could be, with Pereira’s side preparing for a last-16 Europa League tie against Danish club Midtjylland.

However, many supporters would probably happily accept a finale to the campaign with as little drama as possible — and the chance to watch their side play top-flight football again from next August, irrespective of the cost.
